text:
zoe: Quick question  Our baby was born overseas on 2026-06-01 and we flew back last week. Embassy said passport will be ~6-8 weeks. Can I enroll and make coverage effective to DOB without an SSN or final passport?
noah-benefits: Short answer: yes, enroll now and we can make coverage effective to the DOB if you report within the 30-day QLE window. SSN and final passport/CRBA can be provided later.
zoe: What docs should I upload? hospital paperwork is in Spanish and embassy gave an interim travel doc.
noah-benefits: For provisional enrollment we accept any TWO of: 1) hospital newborn record, 2) embassy/consulate travel letter or interim travel document, 3) local birth certificate (certified translation ok), 4) infant passport when available. If translated docs are used, a certified translation is sufficient  apostille not required for our intake.
peopleops-lina: Also, if the child's name or DOB differs slightly between docs, include a short note explaining and we can annotate the file.
dave-payroll: Heads up on payroll: when benefits sets effective date to DOB we'll do a retro premium reconciliation in the next pay cycle after benefits processes. That could be a deduction or a credit depending on pay timing. If you want us to spread any large adjustment, we can split it across two runs on request.
zoe: SSN timeline  embassy said SSN appointment could be separate and slow. Is SSN required to enroll?
noah-benefits: Not required to enroll. We ask for SSN within 60 days if you want dependent tax-free coverage for certain accounts (dependent care FSA rules). If no SSN in 60 days, we still enroll but benefits verification vendor may follow up.
zoe: Verification vendor? Should I expect a separate audit?
noah-benefits: We use an external verification vendor occasionally for dependent audits. If they request docs later, we'll notify you via the case and Slack thread. Keep final documents (CRBA/passport/SSN) handy to upload to the same case.
benefits-bot: Enrollment guide: https://hr.redwood.example/newborns-intl (includes checklist + upload steps). Processing SLA: 3-7 business days after complete docs.
zoe: Where exactly do I upload the provisional docs? I tried the portal but could not find the right event label.
noah-benefits: Steps: HR Portal > Benefits > Report a Life Event > "Add dependent  newborn/placement (QLE)" > Enter DOB: 2026-06-01 > Attach files (multiple allowed) > In notes write: "Born abroad  interim embassy travel doc + hospital record attached. Passport/CRBA pending; will upload when available." Or open a case and cc benefits@redwood.example.
zoe: Thanks. Any difference for dental/vision?
noah-benefits: Dental/vision toggles are separate; make sure to check those boxes if you want them added. We can add them retroactive under the same QLE.
dave-payroll: If you have HSA contributions, and you switch plans when adding dependent, ping payroll after benefits confirms so we can adjust pre-tax deductions and YTD amounts.
zoe: Got it. Uploading now and will drop the case number here. Really appreciate the quick help :heart:
